title: GPA Calculation Methodology
overview: Grade Point Average (GPA) measures academic performance by assigning numeric values to letter grades and computing a weighted average. Different scales (4.0, 5.0) and weighting methods exist.

methods.name: Standard 4.0 Scale
methods.description: The most common GPA scale in the US. Letter grades are converted to points (A=4, B=3, C=2, D=1, F=0) and averaged by credit hours.

formula.name: Weighted Average GPA
formula.expression: GPA = Σ(Grade Points × Credit Hours) / Σ(Credit Hours)

methods.bestFor: College GPA, unweighted high school GPA

methods.name: Weighted GPA (5.0+ Scale)
methods.description: Adds bonus points for honors, AP, or IB courses. A in AP class might be worth 5.0 instead of 4.0.
limitations: Colleges often recalculate on their own scale
methods.bestFor: High school rankings, course rigor recognition

methods.name: Cumulative GPA
methods.description: Overall GPA across all semesters/terms, accounting for varying credit loads.

formula.name: Cumulative Calculation
formula.expression:
Cum. GPA = Σ(All Grade Points × All Credit Hours) / Σ(All Credit Hours)

Or: New Cum. = (Old Cum. × Old Hours + New GPA × New Hours) / Total Hours

sources.name: US Department of Education - Academic Standards

footnotes: Cum laude: ~3.5+, Magna cum laude: ~3.7+, Summa cum laude: ~3.9+
International scales vary widely (UK, Europe use different systems)
disclaimer: GPA scales and weighting methods vary by institution. Check your school's specific policies for accurate calculation.
